title: Existing participant map is deleted before replacement generation succeeds
reasoning: The command removes the current FastParticipantMap unconditionally, then starts asynchronous generation. If the Celery task fails, is never picked up, or returns a non-success result, the previously working map has already been deleted and the command only prints an error when --wait is used. Without --wait, the command reports background generation and exits after deleting the old map, so users can be left with no map at all.
recommendation: Generate the replacement first and only swap/delete the old map after success, or make the task update the existing row transactionally. If deletion is required for correctness, preserve enough state to restore or fail before deleting when the task cannot be queued.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are listed for this feature, and the excerpt does not show coverage for task failure or queue failure after an existing map is present.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create an existing FastParticipantMap, mock generate_participant_map.delay or the task result to fail, run regenerate_map, and assert the original map remains available and the command reports failure.
minimumFixScope: Change regenerate_map so destructive deletion happens only after successful replacement generation or is handled atomically by the generation workflow.
